title: Critical Java4Shell flaw allows RCE attacks on major Java applications
content_md: A critical vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell in OpenJDK, the open-source implementation of Java, can allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on popular enterprise applications, including Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. Java is one of the most widely used programming platforms in the world, powering enterprise applications, web services, financial systems, and critical business infrastructure. Because many applications use the same Java runtime, vulnerabilities in its core components can affect a wide range of different and unrelated applications. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 , is a memory-corruption flaw in Java's hardware-accelerated Base64 decoding functionality that can be exploited to disclose sensitive information from memory or achieve remote code execution (RCE). Security researchers at Calif, who disclosed the flaw on Tuesday, rated it critical with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2, while Oracle assigned it a lower severity rating of 8.1 (High) using CVSS 3.1. Java4Shell affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, as well as Java distributions built from the affected code, including Oracle Java SE, Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, and Red Hat OpenJDK. The vulnerability stems from a bug in Java's Base64 decoder, which processes encoded data commonly found in authentication, file uploads, and network communications.
